verdict: OK to lend in Ludhiana bicycles & parts — back assemblers and component makers with GST-paid turnover and a funded working-capital cycle; skip loss-making, export-dependent names.
title: Ludhiana Bicycles & Parts: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**Ludhiana's bicycle cluster turns steel tube, strip and bought-out components into frames, forks, rims and complete cycles, and cash comes back only after the dealer or OEM pays.** The value sits in the assembly line and the brand, not in the steel — so the borrower's real asset is its order book and its dealer network, not its shed. Cost is dominated by steel and components; pricing power is thin because a cycle is a commodity and the buyer compares three quotes. Working capital is the whole game: steel must be bought and paid for before a cycle is sold, so the cycle is long and the bank funds it. Capex is modest — a paint line or a welding jig — so a proposal asking for large term debt for 'expansion' deserves a hard look at what is actually being bought.

## What has changed now
**The local signal is a working-capital squeeze, not a demand collapse.** Ludhiana industry has asked for GST on steel to be cut to 5% specifically to ease the MSME working-capital crunch [2], and CICU has taken time-bound GST refunds and manufacturing-friendly reform to the CBIC Chairman [1]. Read that plainly: **refunds are slow and input credit is stuck, so the borrower's cash is parked with the government, not with us.** The demand side is better — the Khelo India sports goods manufacturing scheme has been approved and bicycle-industry stakeholders in Ludhiana have welcomed it [3]. On the national read, IIP for NIC 30 is +25.3% YoY and +22.7% Apr-to-date, while bank credit is +27.0% YoY, a gap of +4.3 pp [D] — **credit is running ahead of output, so some of what we are being asked to fund is inventory build, not sales.** Punjab GST is +9.7% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1% [D], a genuine local tailwind. Peer read: Tube Investments' bicycle segment revenue rose to 194 crores from 168 crores, with total revenue +11.5% [4][5] — but that is a 2025 call and is old; treat it as direction, not current fact. Atlas Cycles is reported loss-making with declining revenue [7].

## Where to grow
**Pursue component and frame makers selling to organised OEMs, and assemblers with a domestic dealer network and GST-paid turnover.** The Khelo India scheme approval [3] points to sports-goods adjacencies — cycle pumps, helmets, fitness equipment — and those borrowers are worth a call now. **Avoid pure export assemblers and anyone whose numbers only work at a steel price they do not control**; Atlas's loss-making, revenue-declining profile [7] is the shape of that borrower. When a proposal lands, check the GST return against the sales figure; if the gap is more than a month's sales, ask where the difference sits.

## How to grow safely
**Structure as a cash-flow loan against a drawing power built on paid GST invoices, not on stock statements alone.** Take the steel purchase register and the dealer ledger every month, plus GST 2A/2B reconciliation — that is where the refund delay [1][2] will show up first. Covenant on total debt to operating profit and on gearing, per the rating methodology [10]. If the borrower cannot show a funded cycle shorter than its stated credit period, ask for the debtor ageing before sanction.

## Early warning signs
**Watch the GST refund receivable and the steel creditor days together — when refunds slow and creditors shorten, the borrower is funding the government and the mill at once.** A dealer who moves from advance to credit, or a shift from OEM supply to unbranded local sale, is the next signal. If monthly GST payment falls while sales hold, ask for the e-way bill data.
watch: input credit gap widens two months running -> cut drawing power
creditors shorten while stock holds -> ask for cash-flow statement
dealer credit period lengthens -> reprice or reduce limit
payment falls while sales hold -> stop fresh disbursal
OEM orders drop two quarters -> review limit
watch_note: Trigger levels are policy suggestions (analytical framing), not data.
news_why: Local GST refund and steel-cost squeeze offset by scheme approval and faster Punjab GST growth.
